question: A 71-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus comes to the physician because of a 9-month history of pain and stiffness in the right knee. He reports that the stiffness lasts approximately 10 minutes after waking up and that the pain is worse in the evening. There is no history of trauma. He is 175 cm (5 ft 9 in) tall and weighs 102 kg (225 lb); BMI is 33 kg/m2. Examination of the right knee shows tenderness in the anteromedial joint line and crepitus during knee movement. Laboratory studies show an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 15 mm/h and a serum uric acid concentration of 6.9 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely finding on imaging of the right knee?

options.opa: Osteophytes and narrowing of the joint-space
options.opb: Marginal bony erosions and opacification of periarticular soft tissue
options.opd: Loculated epiphyseal cyst with thinning of the overlying cortex
options.ope: Bony ankylosis and bone proliferation at the entheses

analysis: The patient's presentation is consistent with osteoarthritis, given his age, history of diabetes, morning stiffness lasting less than 30 minutes, pain worse in the evening, tenderness in the joint line, and crepitus. The most likely finding on imaging of the right knee in osteoarthritis would be osteophytes and narrowing of the joint-space.
